issue.title: widget state not synced between multiple pages
issue.body:
### Summary

I noticed that the widget state for inputs with same keys is not synced when switching pages.
This comes a bit surprising with the [documented](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/get-started/multipage-apps#notes) and observed  shared session state.

### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-4989)

Code snippet:

- index.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write(st.session_state)
```
- pages/a.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write('st.session_state', st.session_state)
st.text_input('inp', key='shared_input')
```
- pages/b.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write('st.session_state', st.session_state)
st.text_input('inp', key='shared_input')
```

(Please provide a code snippet! This will help expedite us finding and solving the problem.)

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Run `streamlit run index.py`
2. Click on Page A
3. Enter text into input
4. Click on Page B
5. See preserved session state, but empty input widget

**Expected behavior:**

Widgets with same user keys should be synced when switching pages.

**Actual behavior:**

Widget state goes out-of-sync with session state.

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
no

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.11.0
- Python version: 3.10.0
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Nope
- OS version: Fedora 36
- Browser version: Brave/Chrome

### Additional information

Current **workaround** is to explicitly copy over the previous' page widget state into the session state to populate widgets using the same keys.
```py
st.session_state.update(st.session_state)
```

To not force widgets to invalid selections, our actually used workaround only does so on page navigation.

```py
if ctx := get_script_run_ctx():
    new_page = ctx.page_script_hash
else:
    logger.warning('Missing streamlit context')
    new_page = 'unknown'

old_page = st.session_state.get('_page_script_hash')

if new_page != old_page:
    # https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4989
    st.session_state.update(st.session_state)

st.session_state['_page_script_hash'] = new_page
```

Also see:
- [Session State and Widget State association](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state#session-state-and-widget-state-association)
- [An option to keep component values in the session state · Issue #4458 · streamlit/streamlit](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4458)
- [Preserve widget state when a widget disappears from the page (demoed via Multipage Apps) · Issue #5813](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5813).

comments.body: @MartinNowak thanks for reporting this issue! I was able to reproduce it and have deployed a version [here](https://lukasmasuch-st-playground-issuesgh-4989app-z0dekf.streamlitapp.com/). There is indeed an issue related to the widget state which is cleared up after the widgets get removed. This has a negative side effect in combination with multipage apps. The workaround works since `st.session_state[key] = val` stores the value differently compared to the widget state value.

I appear to have a similar bug with the pages in the sidebar. My multipage app currently uses authentification with multiple users (I used [this guide](https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/deploy/authentication-without-sso)). When I authentify, I land on my Home page. However, when I click on one of my pages (either page 1 or 2), the script reloads the Home page instead of loading the page. When I click a second time, the page loads correctly, and the behavior disappears.

This leads me to think that it is related to the session state variables generated by the check_password function.

The beginning of my Home page : 

```python
import os
import toml
import streamlit as st
if check_password():
    QUESTIONS_YAML = st.secrets["data"]["yaml_questions_path"]
    TRANSLATION_YAML = st.secrets["data"]["yaml_translation_path"]
    st.session_state["questions_mapping"] = toml.load(QUESTIONS_YAML)
    st.session_state["translation_mapping"] = toml.load(TRANSLATION_YAML)
    st.session_state["api_forms"], st.session_state["api_sheets"] = None, None
    if not os.path.exists("data"):
        os.mkdir("data")
```

The beginning of my page 1 : 

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from analyser.streamlit_helpers import check_password
from analyser.df_processing import generate_value_counts_df
from Home import FORMS_CSV_PATH, MULTI_CHOICE_COLUMNS, COLUMN_NAMES_RENAMING_DICT

if check_password():
    available_columns = COLUMN_NAMES_RENAMING_DICT.values()
    converter_dict = {i: pd.eval for i in MULTI_CHOICE_COLUMNS}
    df_full = pd.read_csv(FORMS_CSV_PATH, sep=";", converters=converter_dict)
    selected_column = st.selectbox(
        "Choose a variable to see the answer count",
        available_columns,
    )
```

@louistransfer The issue in your case for this behavior might be that you are importing the home module:

```python
from Home import ...
```

This will automatically run the module script and execute all `st` commands in home the first time the module is loaded.
Thanks a lot @LukasMasuch, importing all necessary variables in the session state instead of importing the Home module fixed my reloading issue.

Same issue here. Kind of a showstopper . For me the only working solution is to duplicate the widget values into  a new session_state variable (dict) and reassign the widget values at the beginning of the page like so: 

```python
import streamlit as st
import random

if 'init' not in st.session_state: # a first run init!
    st.session_state.init = True # not related to any widget. Thats why it is preserved!
    st.session_state.store = {} # not related to a widget -> preserved!
    st.session_state.store['my_number'] = st.session_state.my_number = 1    

st.session_state.my_number = st.session_state.store['my_number'] #recreate widget value

def form_callback():
    st.session_state.my_number += 1*(0.5-random.random())
    st.session_state.store['my_number'] = st.session_state.my_number
    
with st.form(key='my_form'):    
    st.number_input('number',key='my_number')
    submit_button = st.form_submit_button(label='modify values!', on_click=form_callback)
```

@MartinNowak there's a typo in the workaround, could you update the issue description with `.items()`:
> ```python
> for key, val in st.session_state.items():
>   st.session_state[key] = val
> ```

UPDATE: I found the simpler syntax:
```python
st.session_state.update(st.session_state)
```

However, this workaround creates another annoying issue: Thowing warnings in the UI:
*The widget with key "mykey" was created with a default value but also had its value set via the Session State API.*
This requies each widget to be set initially with
```python
if "mykey" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.mykey= myval
```
and remove the `value=` param of the widget. Quite an annoyance.
Streamlit team is looking at how to improve / change this behavior. If you have other thoughts or examples beyond what's already discussed here, please let us know over in #6074

I'm going to close this as a duplicate so the tracking is clearer. There are two issues here:

1. By design, Streamlit today doesn't provide a built-in way to persist widget state across pages / re-runs. We're considering a feature to improve this, see #6074
2. There's a bug currently where identically defined widgets on different pages will show inconsistent results between what's displayed and what's in session_state when you switch pages - #6146. This is a bug, we should fix it.

I am hoping we can address both of these (particularly 2) in the near future!
